records.literal_gloss: And spoke God all the these words, saying,

en.L: And God spoke all these words, saying,
en.B: God spoke all these words, and said,
en.R: Then God spoke these words to the people:

es.L: Y Dios pronunció todas estas palabras, diciendo:
es.B: Dios dio a conocer todas estas palabras y dijo:
es.R: Entonces Dios le dijo al pueblo estas palabras:

fr.L: Et Dieu prononça toutes ces paroles, disant :
fr.B: Dieu fit entendre toutes ces paroles ; il dit :
fr.R: Alors Dieu a dit ces paroles au peuple :

sw.L: Na Mungu akayatamka maneno haya yote, akisema,
sw.B: Mungu aliyatamka maneno haya yote, akasema,
sw.R: Kisha Mungu akawaambia watu maneno haya:

decisions.choice: all these words: the Ten Words, spoken by God himself
decisions.reason: Scripture calls what follows "the ten words" (34:28; Deuteronomy 4:13; 10:4). They are given as God's own speech, heard by the whole people from the mountain (verses 19 and 22; Deuteronomy 5:4, 22), before the laws given through Moses (verse 22 onward).

decisions.choice: saying: introduces the words that follow
decisions.reason: The word marks the start of a quotation. The speech runs from verse 2 to verse 17.

decisions.choice: to the people
decisions.reason: Readable names who heard the words: the people gathered at the foot of the mountain (19:17, 25; verse 19).

decisions.choice: passé simple (L, B: "prononça", "fit entendre"); passé composé (R: "a dit")
decisions.reason: As the French style guide sets for narrative. The narration of this chapter is short (verses 1 and 18-22); God's words keep the tenses of speech at every level, so the past tenses inside them (verses 2, 11, 22) are passé composé throughout.

records.literal_gloss: I [am] Yahweh your God, who brought you out from [the] land of Egypt, from a house of slaves.

en.L: "I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt, from the house of slaves.
en.B: "I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. I brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house where you were slaves.
en.R: "I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. I brought you out of Egypt, where you lived as slaves.

es.L: «Yo [soy] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios, que te hice salir de la tierra de Egipto, de la casa de esclavos.
es.B: «Yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios. Fui yo quien te sacó del país de Egipto, de la casa en que servías como esclavo.
es.R: «Yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios. Yo te rescaté de Egipto, donde vivías como esclavo.

fr.L: « Je [suis] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu, qui t’ai fait sortir du pays d’Égypte, de la maison des esclaves.
fr.B: « Je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu. C’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} qui t’ai fait sortir du pays d’Égypte, de la maison où tu servais comme esclave.
fr.R: « Je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu. Je t’ai fait sortir d’Égypte, où tu vivais comme esclave.

sw.L: "Mimi [ni] {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako, ambaye nilikutoa kutoka nchi ya Misri, kutoka nyumba ya watumwa.
sw.B: "Mimi ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako. Nilikuleta nje ya nchi ya Misri, kutoka nyumba ulimotumikishwa kama mtumwa.
sw.R: "Mimi ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako. Nilikutoa Misri, ulikoishi ukiwa mtumwa.

decisions.choice: I am Yahweh your God: God names himself before he commands
decisions.reason: The words can also be read "I, Yahweh, am your God". Either way God first says who he is and what he has done; the commands that follow rest on that rescue (6:6-7; 19:4).

decisions.choice: house of slaves: Egypt as the place of slavery
decisions.reason: The phrase pictures Egypt as a household where Israel served as slaves (13:3, 14; Deuteronomy 5:6; 7:8).

decisions.choice: the ten words are counted in more than one way
alternatives: verses 3-6 are one word, and verse 17 two
decisions.reason: Scripture says there are ten (34:28; Deuteronomy 4:13) but does not number them, and communities have long divided them differently. Jewish tradition counts this verse as the first word and verses 3-6 as the second. Another ancient count, followed by Orthodox and most Protestant churches, makes verse 3 the first and verses 4-6 the second. A third, followed by Roman Catholic and Lutheran churches, joins verses 3-6 as the first and divides the coveting of verse 17 into two. The words themselves are the same in every count.

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: "Slaves" at every level, as the style guide keeps it for Israel's slavery in Egypt, "the house of slavery" (m2).

decisions.choice: nyumba ya watumwa (L); nyumba ulimotumikishwa kama mtumwa (B); ulikoishi ukiwa mtumwa (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture with the plural noun "watumwa" (slaves), as the Hebrew and the English Literal have; Balanced and Readable say that Israel itself lived there as a slave (m2). "Mtumwa" at every level, as for slavery in Egypt.

source.text: לֹֽ֣א יִהְיֶֽה־לְךָ֛אֱלֹהִ֥יםאֲחֵרִ֖יםעַל־פָּנָֽיַ

records.literal_gloss: Not will be to you other gods on my face.

en.L: There shall not be for you other gods before {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face.
en.B: You shall have no other gods besides {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: Do not have any other gods except {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: No habrá para ti otros dioses delante de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} rostro.
es.B: No tendrás ningún otro dios aparte de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.R: Fuera de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, no tengas ningún otro dios.

fr.L: Il n’y aura pas pour toi d’autres dieux devant {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} face.
fr.B: Tu n’auras aucun autre dieu à côté de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.R: N’aie aucun autre dieu que {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.

sw.L: Hakutakuwa kwako miungu mingine mbele ya uso {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}.
sw.B: Hutakuwa na mungu mwingine yeyote kando {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}.
sw.R: Mungu wako ni {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} tu; usiwe na mwingine.

decisions.choice: on my face: besides me, in my presence
decisions.reason: The phrase is literally "on my face". It may mean "besides me" (no other god alongside Yahweh), "in my presence" (nowhere where God sees, which is everywhere), or "in defiance of me". Each reading forbids Israel any god but Yahweh.

decisions.choice: other gods: no rival may share Israel's loyalty
decisions.reason: The command does not argue about what other gods are; it forbids Israel to have them. Israel belongs to Yahweh alone (22:19; 23:13; 34:14).

decisions.choice: Do not ... (Readable); You shall not ... (Literal, Balanced)
decisions.reason: The commands use the form of a lasting prohibition. Literal and Balanced say "You shall not"; Readable uses the plain "Do not" throughout this chapter. No level uses "thou shalt".

decisions.choice: future at L and B ("no tendrás", "no harás"); negative imperative at R ("no tengas", "no hagas")
decisions.reason: The ten words use the Hebrew form of a lasting prohibition. Spanish says it with the future at Literal and Balanced; Readable uses the plain negative imperative, as the English Readable says "Do not". The same forms are used throughout the chapter and for Deuteronomy 5.

decisions.choice: future with "ne ... pas" at L and B ("tu n'auras pas", "tu ne feras pas"); imperative at R ("n'aie pas", "ne fais pas")
decisions.reason: French says a lasting prohibition with the future. "Ne ... point" is dated, as "thou shalt not" is in English, so no level uses it. Readable uses the imperative, as the English Readable says "Do not". The same forms are used throughout the chapter and for Deuteronomy 5.

decisions.choice: -ta- future with the negative ("hutakuwa", "hutafanya") or the negative subjunctive ("usifanye") at L and B; the negative subjunctive at R ("usiwe", "usiibe")
alternatives: the negative subjunctive at every level
decisions.reason: Swahili commands use the negative subjunctive, and the short prohibitions of verses 13-15 keep it at every level since it is the only natural form. In the longer commands Literal and Balanced often use the -ta- future ("you shall not"); Readable uses the plain negative subjunctive, as the English Readable says "Do not".

records.literal_gloss: Not you shall make for yourself a carved image and any form which [is] in the heavens above and which [is] on the earth beneath and which [is] in the waters under the earth.

en.L: You shall not make for yourself a carved image, or any form that [is] in the heavens above, or that [is] on the earth beneath, or that [is] in the waters under the earth.
en.B: You shall not make yourself a carved idol, nor a figure of anything in the heavens overhead, on the earth below, or in the waters beneath the earth.
en.R: Do not make any idol for yourself. Do not make a statue or a picture of anything in the sky, on the land, or in the water below the land.

es.L: No te harás imagen tallada, ni forma alguna de lo que [está] en los cielos arriba, o de lo que [está] en la tierra abajo, o de lo que [está] en las aguas bajo la tierra.
es.B: No te fabricarás ningún ídolo tallado, ni figura de cosa alguna que haya allá arriba en los cielos, aquí abajo en la tierra o en las aguas por debajo de la tierra.
es.R: No te fabriques ningún ídolo. No hagas estatuas ni imágenes de nada que haya en el cielo, en la tierra o en el agua debajo de la tierra.

fr.L: Tu ne te feras pas d’image sculptée, ni aucune forme de ce qui [est] dans les cieux en haut, ou de ce qui [est] sur la terre en bas, ou de ce qui [est] dans les eaux sous la terre.
fr.B: Tu ne te fabriqueras pas d’idole taillée, ni la figure de quoi que ce soit qui se trouve là-haut dans le ciel, ici-bas sur la terre ou dans les eaux au-dessous de la terre.
fr.R: Ne te fabrique aucune idole. Ne fais ni statue ni image de quoi que ce soit dans le ciel, sur la terre, ou dans l’eau sous la terre.

sw.L: Hutajifanyia sanamu ya kuchonga, wala umbo lolote la kitu kilicho katika mbingu juu, au kilicho katika nchi chini, au kilicho katika maji chini ya nchi.
sw.B: Hutajitengenezea sanamu iliyochongwa, wala sura ya kitu chochote kilichoko mbinguni juu, katika ardhi chini, au ndani ya maji yaliyo chini ya ardhi.
sw.R: Usijitengenezee sanamu ya kuabudu. Usichonge wala usichore kitu chochote kilicho angani, juu ya nchi kavu, au ndani ya maji chini ya nchi.

decisions.choice: carved image: an idol shaped by a craftsman
decisions.reason: The word comes from a verb meaning to cut or carve. It names an image of wood or stone made to be worshiped (Deuteronomy 7:25; Isaiah 44:15-17), and later idols of any kind.

decisions.choice: any form: no image of anything, including of Yahweh himself
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 4:15-18 gives the reason: Israel saw no form when Yahweh spoke from the fire, so they must make no image of anything. The command forbids images of other gods and also any image meant to stand for Yahweh (32:4-5).

decisions.choice: heavens, earth, waters under the earth: the whole created world
decisions.reason: The three parts name everything there is: birds and the lights of the sky, land animals and people, and fish (Deuteronomy 4:16-19). The waters "under the earth" are the seas and waters lower than the land.

decisions.choice: idol ... statue or a picture
decisions.reason: Readable says "idol" and spells out "form" as a statue or a picture, things made to be worshiped.

decisions.choice: Usichonge wala usichore (do not carve or draw)
decisions.reason: Readable spells out "statue or picture" with the two verbs for making them, which reads more plainly in Swahili than two nouns after one verb.

records.literal_gloss: Not you shall bow down to them and not you shall be made to serve them, for I, Yahweh your God, [am] a jealous God, visiting [the] iniquity of fathers on children, on [the] third and on [the] fourth of those who hate me,

en.L: You shall not bow down to them, and you shall not serve them; for I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, [am] a jealous God, visiting [the] iniquity of fathers upon children, upon [the] third and upon [the] fourth [generation] of those who hate {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}},
en.B: You shall neither bow to them nor serve them. For I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, am a jealous God. I bring the guilt of fathers upon their children, upon the third and the fourth generation of those who hate {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}},
en.R: Do not bow down to them or serve them. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and I am a jealous God. I will not share your loyalty with other gods. When people hate {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, I punish their sin, even in their grandchildren and great-grandchildren.

es.L: No te postrarás ante ellas, y no las servirás; porque yo, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios, [soy] un Dios celoso, que visita la iniquidad de los padres sobre los hijos, sobre la tercera y sobre la cuarta [generación] de los que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} odian,
es.B: No te inclinarás ante ellos ni les rendirás culto. Pues yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios, un Dios celoso. Hago caer la culpa de los padres sobre sus hijos, sobre la tercera y la cuarta generación de los que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} odian,
es.R: No te arrodilles ante ellos ni les sirvas. Yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios, y soy un Dios celoso: no permito que tu lealtad sea también para otros dioses. Cuando alguien {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} odia, castigo su pecado, aun en sus nietos y bisnietos.

fr.L: Tu ne te prosterneras pas devant elles, et tu ne les serviras pas ; car {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu, [je suis] un Dieu jaloux, qui visite la faute des pères sur les fils, sur la troisième et sur la quatrième [génération] de ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} haïssent,
fr.B: Tu ne t’inclineras pas devant elles et tu ne leur rendras pas de culte. Je suis en effet {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu, un Dieu jaloux. Je fais retomber la faute des pères sur leurs enfants, sur la troisième et la quatrième génération de ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} haïssent,
fr.R: Ne te prosterne pas devant elles et ne les sers pas. Je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu, et je suis un Dieu jaloux : je ne veux pas que ta fidélité soit partagée avec d’autres dieux. Quand des gens {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} haïssent, je punis leur péché, même chez leurs petits-enfants et leurs arrière-petits-enfants.

sw.L: Hutavisujudia, wala hutavitumikia; kwa maana {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako, [ni] Mungu mwenye wivu, ninayeadhibu uovu wa baba juu ya watoto, juu ya [kizazi cha] tatu na juu ya [kizazi cha] nne cha wale wanaonichukia,
sw.B: Hutavisujudia wala kuvitumikia. Kwa maana ndimi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako, Mungu mwenye wivu. Ninaleta hatia ya baba juu ya watoto wao, juu ya vizazi vya tatu na vya nne vya wale wanaonichukia,
sw.R: Usizisujudie sanamu hizo wala kuzitumikia. Mimi ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} ni Mungu mwenye wivu. Sitakubali uaminifu wako ugawanywe na miungu mingine. Watu wanaponichukia, ninaiadhibu dhambi yao, hata kwa wajukuu wao na vitukuu vyao.

decisions.choice: jealous: passionate, demanding sole loyalty
decisions.reason: The word describes a strong, burning claim on someone who belongs to you, like a husband's claim on his wife's faithfulness. It is not petty envy. God will not share his people's worship with any other god; in 34:14 "Jealous" is even called his name (Deuteronomy 4:24; 6:15).

decisions.choice: visiting iniquity to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me: judgment that reaches a family that keeps hating God
alternatives: punishing the children for the sin of their fathers
decisions.reason: To "visit" is to attend to, here to punish. Three or four generations could live in one household, so the sin of the head of the house would reach all who lived under it. "Those who hate me" may describe the fathers or the children who follow them in it. The law did not punish children for their parents' crimes in court (Deuteronomy 24:16; Ezekiel 18:20).

decisions.choice: serve them: the verb has an unusual form
decisions.reason: The vowels of the verb give a form that may mean "be made to serve them" or "be led into serving them". The sense is the same: Israel must not worship idols.

decisions.choice: grandchildren and great-grandchildren
decisions.reason: Counting the fathers as the first generation, the third and fourth are their grandchildren and great-grandchildren. Readable says so, and adds "I will not share your loyalty" to explain "jealous".

decisions.choice: un Dios celoso
alternatives: un Dios que exige lealtad total
decisions.reason: "Celoso" is the word for a husband's rightful claim on his wife's faithfulness, the picture behind the Hebrew (m1). It is kept at every level; Readable adds what it means, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: un Dieu jaloux
decisions.reason: "Jaloux" keeps the picture of a husband's claim on his wife's faithfulness (m1). Readable adds what it means, as the English Readable does, so that it is not read as petty envy.

decisions.choice: Mungu mwenye wivu
decisions.reason: "Wivu" is the word for a spouse's claim on faithfulness, the picture behind the Hebrew (m1). Readable adds what it means, as the English Readable does.

source.text: וְעֹ֥שֶׂהחֶ֖סֶדלַאֲלָפִ֑יםלְאֹהֲבַ֖י וּלְשֹׁמְרֵ֥י מִצְוֺתָֽי׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And doing covenant loyalty to thousands, to those who love me and to those who keep my commandments.

en.L: and doing steadfast love to thousands, to those who love {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and to those who keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments.
en.B: but to thousands who love {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments I show faithful love.
en.R: But to thousands who love {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and obey {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commands, I show faithful love.

es.L: y que obra con amor fiel hacia millares, hacia los que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} aman y hacia los que guardan {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} mandamientos.
es.B: pero a millares de los que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} aman y cumplen {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} mandamientos les muestro {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} amor fiel.
es.R: Pero muestro {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} amor fiel a miles de personas que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} aman y obedecen {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} mandatos.

fr.L: et qui agit avec amour fidèle envers des milliers, envers ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}aiment et envers ceux qui gardent {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} commandements.
fr.B: mais à des milliers de ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}aiment et gardent {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} commandements, je montre un amour fidèle.
fr.R: Mais je reste fidèle dans {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} amour envers des milliers de gens qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}aiment et qui obéissent à {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} commandements.

sw.L: na ninayefanya upendo usiokoma kwa maelfu, kwa wale wanaonipenda na kwa wale wanaozishika amri {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}.
sw.B: lakini maelfu ya wale wanaonipenda na kutii amri {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}} ninawaonyesha upendo wa uaminifu.
sw.R: Lakini maelfu ya watu wanaonipenda na kufuata amri {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}, ninawapenda kwa uaminifu bila kukoma.

decisions.choice: steadfast love: loyal love that keeps covenant
decisions.reason: The same word as in 15:13: kindness that stays true to a bond and acts on it. God shows it to those he has bound himself to (34:6-7).

decisions.choice: thousands: thousands of people, or the thousandth generation
decisions.reason: The word is "thousands". Set against "the third and the fourth" generation in verse 5, it may mean thousands of generations, as Deuteronomy 7:9 says ("to a thousand generations"). Either way God's love far outlasts his judgment.

decisions.choice: those who love me and keep my commandments: loyal covenant partners
decisions.reason: Loving God is shown by keeping what he commands (Deuteronomy 5:10; 7:9; 11:1). These are the opposite of "those who hate me" in verse 5.

decisions.choice: steadfast love (Literal); faithful love (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 15:13 and 34:6-7. Both stress loyalty; words such as "mercy" or "kindness" leave the loyalty out.

decisions.choice: upendo usiokoma (L); upendo wa uaminifu (B); ninawapenda kwa uaminifu bila kukoma (R)
decisions.reason: As the English moves from "steadfast love" to "faithful love", Balanced and Readable name the loyalty in the word. "Rehema" (mercy) and "fadhili" (kindness) leave it out.

source.text: לֹ֥א תִשָּׂ֛א אֶת־שֵֽׁם־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ לַשָּׁ֑וְא כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יְנַקֶּה֙ יְהוָ֔ה אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־יִשָּׂ֥א אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ לַשָּֽׁוְא׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Not you shall lift up [the] name of Yahweh your God to emptiness, for not will leave unpunished Yahweh [the one] who lifts up his name to emptiness.

en.L: You shall not lift up the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God to emptiness, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will not leave unpunished [the one] who lifts up {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name to emptiness.
en.B: You shall not use the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God for what is false or worthless, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will not let anyone go unpunished who uses {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name that way.
en.R: Do not use the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God in false promises or for empty purposes. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will punish anyone who treats {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name like that.

es.L: No alzarás el nombre {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} tu Dios para la vanidad, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no declarará inocente al que alce {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre para la vanidad.
es.B: No usarás el nombre {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} tu Dios para la mentira o para lo que no vale nada, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no dejará sin castigo a nadie que use así {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre.
es.R: No uses el nombre {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} tu Dios en promesas falsas ni para cosas sin valor. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} castigará a cualquiera que trate {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre de esa manera.

fr.L: Tu ne lèveras pas le nom {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ton Dieu pour le vide, car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ne tiendra pas pour innocent celui qui lève {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom pour le vide.
fr.B: Tu n’utiliseras pas le nom {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ton Dieu pour le mensonge ou pour rien, car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ne laissera sans punition personne qui se sert ainsi de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom.
fr.R: N’utilise pas le nom {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ton Dieu dans de fausses promesses ou pour des choses vaines. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} punira toute personne qui traite {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom de cette façon.

sw.L: Hutaliinua jina la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako kwa ubatili, kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hatamwacha bila adhabu yule aliinuaye jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} kwa ubatili.
sw.B: Hutalitumia jina la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako kwa uongo au kwa mambo yasiyo na maana, kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hatamwachilia mtu yeyote anayelitumia jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} hivyo bila kumwadhibu.
sw.R: Usilitumie jina la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako katika ahadi za uongo au kwa mambo yasiyo na faida. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atamwadhibu kila mtu anayelitendea jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} hivyo.

decisions.choice: lift up the name to emptiness: use God's name falsely or for nothing
decisions.reason: To "lift up" the name is to speak it, above all in an oath (Psalm 24:4; Leviticus 19:12). "Emptiness" means what is false or worthless (Deuteronomy 5:20 uses it of false witness). The command forbids swearing falsely by God's name, and any use of it that treats it as empty: in lies, curses or magic.

decisions.choice: will not leave unpunished: will not acquit
decisions.reason: The verb means to declare clean or innocent. God will treat the one who misuses his name as guilty (34:7).

decisions.choice: for what is false or worthless / in false promises or for empty purposes
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out both senses of "emptiness". Literal keeps the picture.

source.text: זָכ֛וֹראֶת־י֥וֹםהַשַּׁבָּ֖תלְקַדְּשֽׁוֹ

records.literal_gloss: Remember the day of the Sabbath, to make it holy.

en.L: Remember the day of the Sabbath, to make it holy.
en.B: Remember the Sabbath day and set it apart as holy.
en.R: Remember the Sabbath day. Treat it as a holy day.

es.L: Recuerda el día del sábado, para hacerlo santo.
es.B: Acuérdate del día sábado y apártalo como santo.
es.R: Recuerda el sábado. Trátalo como un día santo.

fr.L: Souviens-toi du jour du sabbat, pour le rendre saint.
fr.B: Rappelle-toi le jour du sabbat et mets-le à part comme saint.
fr.R: Pense au jour du sabbat. Traite-le comme un jour saint.

sw.L: Kumbuka siku ya Sabato, ili kuifanya takatifu.
sw.B: Kumbuka siku ya Sabato, uitenge iwe takatifu.
sw.R: Usiisahau siku ya Sabato. Iheshimu kama siku takatifu.

decisions.choice: remember: keep in mind and act on it
decisions.reason: To remember is not only to recall but to keep and honor. Deuteronomy 5:12 has "keep" in place of "remember".

decisions.choice: make it holy: set the day apart for God
decisions.reason: The day is to be treated as different from other days, belonging to Yahweh (16:23; 31:14). Verse 11 says God himself made it holy.

decisions.choice: the Sabbath: already given with the manna
decisions.reason: Israel first kept the Sabbath when the manna stopped on the seventh day (16:23-30). Here it becomes one of the ten words.

source.text: שֵׁ֤שֶׁתיָמִים֙תַּֽעֲבֹ֔דוְעָשִׂ֖יתָכָּל־מְלַאכְתֶּֽךָ

records.literal_gloss: Six days you shall labor and you shall do all your work,

en.L: Six days you shall labor and do all your work,
en.B: You have six days to labor and do all your work,
en.R: You may work for six days and get all your jobs done.

es.L: Seis días te afanarás y harás todo tu trabajo,
es.B: Tienes seis días para trabajar y hacer todas tus tareas,
es.R: Puedes trabajar seis días y terminar todo lo que tengas que hacer.

fr.L: Six jours tu travailleras et tu feras tout ton ouvrage,
fr.B: Tu as six jours pour peiner et accomplir tout ton travail,
fr.R: Tu peux travailler pendant six jours et faire tout ce que tu as à faire.

sw.L: Siku sita utajishughulisha, na utafanya kazi yako yote,
sw.B: Una siku sita za kufanya kazi na kumaliza shughuli zako zote,
sw.R: Unaweza kufanya kazi kwa siku sita na kumaliza kazi zako zote.

decisions.choice: labor: the verb also used for serving
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for Israel's hard service in Egypt (1:13-14) and for serving God (3:12). Six days are for work, the seventh is not.

decisions.choice: do all your work: a permission and a task
decisions.reason: The verse sets the work of the week in its place: there is time enough in six days for all of it.

source.text: וְי֨וֹם֙ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔ישַׁבָּ֖תלַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָלֹֽ֣א־תַעֲשֶׂ֨הכָל־מְלָאכָ֜האַתָּ֣ה׀וּבִנְךָֽ֣־וּבִתֶּ֗ךָעַבְדְּךָ֤וַאֲמָֽתְךָ֙וּבְהֶמְתֶּ֔ךָוְגֵרְךָ֖אֲשֶׁ֥רבִּשְׁעָרֶֽיךָ

records.literal_gloss: And [the] day the seventh [is] a Sabbath to Yahweh your God; not you shall do any work, you and your son and your daughter, your male servant and your female servant and your livestock and your sojourner who [is] in your gates.

en.L: but the seventh day [is] a Sabbath to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. You shall not do any work, you and your son and your daughter, your male servant and your female servant, and your livestock, and your sojourner who [is] within your gates.
en.B: but the seventh day is a Sabbath for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. Do no work on it: not you, nor your son or daughter, nor your male or female servant, nor your livestock, nor the foreigner living among you in your towns.
en.R: But the seventh day is a Sabbath, a day of rest for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. On that day no one in your household may work: not you, not your sons or daughters, not your servants, not your animals, and not the foreigners who live among you in your towns.

es.L: pero el día séptimo [es] sábado para {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios. No harás ningún trabajo, tú y tu hijo y tu hija, tu siervo y tu sierva, y tu ganado, y tu inmigrante que [está] dentro de tus puertas.
es.B: pero el séptimo día es un sábado para {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios. Ese día no hagas ningún trabajo: ni tú, ni tu hijo o tu hija, ni tu siervo o tu sierva, ni tus animales, ni el extranjero que vive contigo en tus ciudades.
es.R: Pero el séptimo día es el sábado, el día de descanso para {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios. Ese día nadie en tu casa debe trabajar: ni tú, ni tus hijos o hijas, ni tus siervos, ni tus animales, ni los extranjeros que viven contigo en tus ciudades.

fr.L: mais le septième jour [est] un sabbat {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} ton Dieu. Tu ne feras aucun ouvrage, toi, et ton fils, et ta fille, ton serviteur et ta servante, et ton bétail, et ton immigré qui [est] dans tes portes.
fr.B: mais le septième jour est un sabbat pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu. Ne fais aucun travail ce jour-là : ni toi, ni ton fils ou ta fille, ni ton serviteur ou ta servante, ni tes bêtes, ni l’étranger qui vit chez toi, dans tes villes.
fr.R: Mais le septième jour est un sabbat, un jour de repos pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu. Ce jour-là, personne dans ta maison ne doit travailler : ni toi, ni tes fils ou tes filles, ni tes serviteurs, ni tes animaux, ni les étrangers qui habitent avec toi dans tes villes.

sw.L: lakini siku ya saba [ni] Sabato kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako. Hutafanya kazi yoyote, wewe na mwana wako na binti yako, mtumishi wako wa kiume na mtumishi wako wa kike, na mifugo yako, na mgeni wako aliye katika malango yako.
sw.B: lakini siku ya saba ni Sabato kwa ajili ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako. Siku hiyo usifanye kazi yoyote, iwe wewe, mwanao au binti yako, mtumishi wako wa kiume au wa kike, mifugo yako, au mgeni anayeishi nawe katika miji yako.
sw.R: Lakini siku ya saba ni Sabato, siku ya kupumzika kwa ajili ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako. Siku hiyo mtu yeyote wa nyumbani mwako asifanye kazi: wewe, watoto wako wa kiume na wa kike, watumishi wako, wanyama wako, hata wageni wanaoishi nawe katika miji yako.

decisions.choice: you, your son, your daughter ... your livestock: the whole household rests
decisions.reason: The command is spoken to the head of a household, who is answerable for everyone under him. Children, servants, working animals and resident foreigners all share the rest. Deuteronomy 5:14-15 adds the reason: "so that your servants may rest as you do", for Israel too was once a slave.

decisions.choice: male servant, female servant: household slaves or bound workers
decisions.reason: The words cover slaves and servants who belonged to the household (21:2-11). They too must be given the day.

decisions.choice: your sojourner within your gates: a foreigner living in your towns
decisions.reason: A sojourner is an outsider who has settled among Israel without land or family rights (12:48-49). "Within your gates" means inside your town.

decisions.choice: the foreigner living among you
decisions.reason: As in 12:48-49, Balanced and Readable say "foreigner living among you"; Literal keeps "sojourner". Readable also adds "a day of rest" to explain the word Sabbath.

source.text: כִּ֣י שֵֽׁשֶׁת־יָמִים֩ עָשָׂ֨ה יְהוָ֜ה אֶת־הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם וְאֶת־הָאָ֗רֶץ אֶת־הַיָּם֙ וְאֶת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֔ם וַיָּ֖נַח בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֑י עַל־כֵּ֗ן בֵּרַ֧ךְ יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־י֥וֹם הַשַּׁבָּ֖ת וַֽיְקַדְּשֵֽׁהוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: For six days made Yahweh the heavens and the earth, the sea and all that [is] in them, and he rested on the day the seventh; therefore blessed Yahweh the day of the Sabbath and made it holy.

en.L: For [in] six days {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made the heavens and the earth, the sea and all that [is] in them, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rested on the seventh day; therefore {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} blessed the day of the Sabbath and made it holy.
en.B: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made the heavens and the earth, the sea and everything in them, in six days, and on the seventh day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rested. For this reason {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} blessed the Sabbath day and made it holy.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} made the sky, the land, the sea and everything in them in six days. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rested on the seventh day. So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} blessed the Sabbath day and made it a holy day.

es.L: Porque [en] seis días {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} hizo los cielos y la tierra, el mar y todo lo que [hay] en ellos, y descansó en el día séptimo; por eso {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} bendijo el día del sábado y lo hizo santo.
es.B: Pues en seis días {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} hizo los cielos y la tierra, el mar y todo cuanto contienen, y el séptimo día descansó. Por esa razón {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} bendijo el día sábado y lo declaró santo.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} hizo el cielo, la tierra, el mar y todo lo que hay en ellos en seis días. Luego descansó el séptimo día. Por eso {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} bendijo el sábado y lo hizo un día santo.

fr.L: Car [en] six jours {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a fait les cieux et la terre, la mer et tout ce qui [est] en eux, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’est reposé le septième jour ; c’est pourquoi {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a béni le jour du sabbat et l’a rendu saint.
fr.B: Car en six jours {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a fait les cieux et la terre, la mer et tout ce qu’ils contiennent, et le septième jour {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’est reposé. Voilà pourquoi {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a béni le jour du sabbat et en a fait un jour saint.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a fait le ciel, la terre, la mer et tout ce qui s’y trouve en six jours. Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’est reposé le septième jour. C’est pour cela que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a béni le jour du sabbat et en a fait un jour saint.

sw.L: Kwa maana [katika] siku sita {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alifanya mbingu na nchi, bahari na kila kitu kilichomo ndani yake, akapumzika katika siku ya saba; kwa sababu hiyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliibariki siku ya Sabato, akaifanya takatifu.
sw.B: Kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alifanya mbingu na dunia, bahari na kila kilichomo ndani yake, kwa siku sita, na siku ya saba akapumzika. Kwa sababu hiyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliibariki siku ya Sabato na kuitakasa.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alifanya anga, nchi, bahari na kila kitu kilichomo kwa siku sita. Kisha akapumzika siku ya saba. Ndiyo maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliibariki siku ya Sabato, akaifanya kuwa siku takatifu.

decisions.choice: in six days ... rested on the seventh: the pattern of creation
decisions.reason: The reason for the Sabbath is taken from Genesis 1:1-2:3, where God made the world in six days and rested on the seventh. Israel's week follows God's. Deuteronomy 5:15 gives a second reason, the rescue from Egypt.

decisions.choice: rested: settled, stopped working
decisions.reason: This verb means to come to rest, to settle. Genesis 2:2-3 says God "ceased", using the word from which Sabbath comes; 31:17 adds that he "was refreshed".

decisions.choice: blessed ... made it holy: as in Genesis 2:3
decisions.reason: The same two verbs are used of the seventh day in Genesis 2:3. The Sabbath is a gift God blessed and a day he set apart.

source.text: כַּבֵּ֥ד אֶת־אָבִ֖יךָ וְאֶת־אִמֶּ֑ךָ לְמַ֨עַן֙ יַאֲרִכ֣וּן יָמֶ֔יךָ עַ֚ל הָאֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ נֹתֵ֥ן לָֽךְ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Honor your father and your mother, so that may be long your days on the land which Yahweh your God [is] giving to you.

en.L: Honor your father and your mother, so that your days may be long upon the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving to you.
en.B: Honor your father and your mother. Then your days will be long in the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is going to give you.
en.R: Honor your father and your mother, and treat them with respect. Then you will enjoy a long life in the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is about to give you.

es.L: Honra a tu padre y a tu madre, para que tus días sean largos sobre el suelo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te está dando.
es.B: Honra a tu padre y a tu madre. Así tus días serán largos en la tierra que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios va a darte.
es.R: Honra a tu padre y a tu madre, y trátalos con respeto. Así vivirás muchos años en la tierra que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios está a punto de darte.

fr.L: Honore ton père et ta mère, afin que tes jours soient longs sur le sol que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu te donne.
fr.B: Honore ton père et ta mère. Ainsi tes jours dureront longtemps dans le pays que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu va te donner.
fr.R: Honore ton père et ta mère, et traite-les avec respect. Alors tu profiteras d’une longue vie dans le pays que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu est sur le point de te donner.

sw.L: Waheshimu baba yako na mama yako, ili siku zako zirefuke juu ya ardhi ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako anakupa.
sw.B: Waheshimu baba yako na mama yako. Ndipo utaishi muda mrefu katika nchi ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako atakupa.
sw.R: Waheshimu baba yako na mama yako, na uwatendee kwa adabu. Ndipo utafurahia maisha marefu katika nchi ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako anakaribia kukupa.

decisions.choice: honor: give weight to, respect and care for
decisions.reason: The verb comes from a root meaning heavy. To honor parents is to treat them as weighty: to respect, obey and care for them, all their lives. Striking or cursing them was a capital crime (21:15, 17; Leviticus 19:3).

decisions.choice: so that your days may be long: a promise attached to the command
decisions.reason: This is the first of the ten words to carry a promise (Deuteronomy 5:16; Ephesians 6:2-3). Long life in the land is a blessing of the covenant (Deuteronomy 4:40).

decisions.choice: the land Yahweh your God is giving you: Canaan, the promised land
decisions.reason: The land promised to Abraham and his descendants (3:8; 6:4, 8). The verb form can mean "is giving" or "is about to give".

source.text: לֹ֖אתִּרְצָֽח

records.literal_gloss: Not you shall murder.

en.L: You shall not murder.
en.B: You shall not murder.
en.R: Do not murder.

es.L: No asesinarás.
es.B: No asesinarás.
es.R: No asesines.

fr.L: Tu ne commettras pas de meurtre.
fr.B: Tu ne commettras pas de meurtre.
fr.R: Ne commets pas de meurtre.

sw.L: Usiue.
sw.B: Usiue.
sw.R: Usimwue mtu.

decisions.choice: murder: the unlawful killing of a person
decisions.reason: This verb is not the general word for killing. It is used only of killing a human being, by intent or by careless violence (Numbers 35:11, 16-21), and never of killing animals or of killing in battle. The law itself orders the death penalty for some crimes (21:12-17), so the command forbids unlawful killing, not all taking of life.

decisions.choice: the verse division follows the source data
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text of the ten words (verses 2-17) carries two sets of accents. One divides the passage into verses of ordinary length; the other treats each commandment as a unit. The two sets divide the verses differently, especially in verses 2-6 and 13-16. The division here follows the source data.

decisions.choice: asesinar
decisions.reason: The verb is used only of unlawful killing of a person, not of all killing (m1). "Asesinar" says that; "matar" (kill) would also cover killing animals, in battle or by lawful sentence.

decisions.choice: commettre un meurtre
decisions.reason: The verb is used only of unlawful killing of a person, not of all killing (m1). "Commettre un meurtre" says that; "tuer" (kill) would also cover killing animals, in battle or by lawful sentence. "Assassiner" would narrow it to planned killing, while the verb also covers careless violence.

decisions.choice: Usimwue mtu (R)
decisions.reason: Swahili has no everyday verb for murder distinct from "kuua" (kill). Literal and Balanced keep the short "Usiue"; Readable adds "mtu" (a person) to show that the command is about killing a human being (m1).

source.text: לֹ֖אתִּנְאָֽף

records.literal_gloss: Not you shall commit adultery.

en.L: You shall not commit adultery.
en.B: You shall not commit adultery.
en.R: Do not commit adultery.

es.L: No cometerás adulterio.
es.B: No cometerás adulterio.
es.R: No cometas adulterio.

fr.L: Tu ne commettras pas d’adultère.
fr.B: Tu ne commettras pas d’adultère.
fr.R: Ne commets pas d’adultère.

sw.L: Usizini.
sw.B: Usizini.
sw.R: Usifanye uzinzi.

decisions.choice: commit adultery: sexual union that breaks a marriage
decisions.reason: The verb is used of sexual relations between a married or betrothed woman and a man who is not her husband, and both were guilty (Leviticus 20:10; Deuteronomy 22:22-24). It guards the marriage bond and the family.

decisions.choice: adultery: later a picture of unfaithfulness to God
decisions.reason: The prophets use the same verb of Israel's turning to other gods (Jeremiah 3:8-9; Hosea 4:13-14), since the covenant is like a marriage.

source.text: לֹ֖אתִּגְנֹֽב

records.literal_gloss: Not you shall steal.

en.L: You shall not steal.
en.B: You shall not steal.
en.R: Do not steal.

es.L: No robarás.
es.B: No robarás.
es.R: No robes.

fr.L: Tu ne voleras pas.
fr.B: Tu ne voleras pas.
fr.R: Ne vole pas.

sw.L: Usiibe.
sw.B: Usiibe.
sw.R: Usiibe.

decisions.choice: steal: take secretly what belongs to another
decisions.reason: The verb covers taking property (22:1-3) and also taking a person: "whoever steals a man" to sell him is to die (21:16; Deuteronomy 24:7).

source.text: לֹֽא־תַעֲנֶ֥ה בְרֵעֲךָ֖ עֵ֥ד שָֽׁקֶר׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Not you shall answer against your neighbor [as] a witness of falsehood.

en.L: You shall not answer against your neighbor [as] a witness of falsehood.
en.B: You shall not give false evidence against your neighbor.
en.R: Do not lie about your neighbor when you are a witness.

es.L: No responderás contra tu prójimo [como] testigo de mentira.
es.B: No declararás en falso contra tu prójimo.
es.R: Cuando seas testigo, no mientas acerca de tu prójimo.

fr.L: Tu ne répondras pas contre ton prochain [comme] témoin de mensonge.
fr.B: Tu ne feras pas de faux témoignage contre ton prochain.
fr.R: Quand tu es témoin, ne mens pas au sujet de ton prochain.

sw.L: Hutajibu dhidi ya jirani yako [kama] shahidi wa uongo.
sw.B: Usitoe ushahidi wa uongo dhidi ya jirani yako.
sw.R: Ukiwa shahidi, usiseme uongo juu ya jirani yako.

decisions.choice: answer as a false witness: testify falsely in court
decisions.reason: To "answer" is the word for giving evidence in a case. A witness who lied could cost a neighbor his property or his life, and was to suffer what he meant to bring on the other (23:1; Deuteronomy 19:16-19). Deuteronomy 5:20 says "a witness of emptiness".

decisions.choice: neighbor: a fellow member of the community
decisions.reason: The word means the person beside you: a fellow Israelite, anyone you deal with (Leviticus 19:18).

decisions.choice: give false evidence / lie ... when you are a witness
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use plain words for the court setting; Literal keeps "answer ... [as] a witness of falsehood".

source.text: לֹ֥א תַחְמֹ֖ד בֵּ֣ית רֵעֶ֑ךָ לֹֽא־תַחְמֹ֞ד אֵ֣שֶׁת רֵעֶ֗ךָ וְעַבְדּ֤וֹ וַאֲמָתוֹ֙ וְשׁוֹר֣וֹ וַחֲמֹר֔וֹ וְכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְרֵעֶֽךָ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Not you shall covet [the] house of your neighbor; not you shall covet [the] wife of your neighbor, and his male servant and his female servant and his ox and his donkey and all that [belongs] to your neighbor.

en.L: You shall not covet the house of your neighbor; you shall not covet the wife of your neighbor, or his male servant, or his female servant, or his ox, or his donkey, or anything that [belongs] to your neighbor."
en.B: You shall not covet your neighbor's household: you shall not set your heart on his wife, his male or female servant, his ox or his donkey, or anything else your neighbor has."
en.R: Do not set your heart on taking your neighbor's household. Do not desire to have his wife, his servants, his ox or donkey, or anything else that belongs to him."

es.L: No codiciarás la casa de tu prójimo; no codiciarás la esposa de tu prójimo, o su siervo, o su sierva, o su buey, o su asno, o cualquier cosa que [pertenezca] a tu prójimo».
es.B: No codiciarás el hogar de tu prójimo: no pondrás los ojos en su esposa, ni en su siervo o su sierva, ni en su buey o su asno, ni en nada más que tenga tu prójimo».
es.R: No pongas tu corazón en quedarte con la casa de tu prójimo. No desees tener a su esposa, sus siervos, su buey o su burro, ni ninguna otra cosa que le pertenezca».

fr.L: Tu ne convoiteras pas la maison de ton prochain ; tu ne convoiteras pas la femme de ton prochain, ou son serviteur, ou sa servante, ou son bœuf, ou son âne, ou quoi que ce soit qui [appartient] à ton prochain. »
fr.B: Tu ne convoiteras pas la maisonnée de ton prochain : tu ne jetteras pas ton dévolu sur sa femme, son serviteur ou sa servante, son bœuf ou son âne, ni sur rien d’autre de ce qu’il possède. »
fr.R: N’aie pas envie de prendre la maison de ton prochain et tout ce qui va avec. Ne cherche pas à avoir sa femme, ses serviteurs, son bœuf ou son âne, ni rien d’autre qui lui appartient. »

sw.L: Hutaitamani nyumba ya jirani yako; hutamtamani mke wa jirani yako, au mtumishi wake wa kiume, au mtumishi wake wa kike, au ng'ombe wake, au punda wake, au chochote [kilicho] cha jirani yako."
sw.B: Hutaitamani nyumba ya jirani yako: usimmezee mate mke wake, wala mtumishi wake wa kiume au wa kike, wala ng'ombe wake au punda wake, wala kitu kingine chochote ambacho ni mali ya jirani yako."
sw.R: Usiwe na tamaa ya kuchukua nyumba ya jirani yako na vyote vilivyomo. Usitamani kuwa na mke wake, watumishi wake, ng'ombe wake au punda wake, wala kitu kingine chochote ambacho ni chake."

decisions.choice: covet: desire what is another's, wanting to take it
decisions.reason: The verb means to desire and delight in something, and with what belongs to another it is the desire that leads to taking it: Achan "coveted them and took them" (Joshua 7:21; Micah 2:2). This word reaches the heart, where the other wrongs begin.

decisions.choice: house: the household, all that follows
decisions.reason: Here "house" means the whole household: the wife, the servants, the animals and everything the neighbor owns, as the rest of the verse lists. Deuteronomy 5:21 names the wife first and uses a different verb for the second "covet".

decisions.choice: set your heart on / desire to have
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats "covet". Balanced says "covet" once and then "set your heart on"; Readable says "set your heart on taking" and "desire to have", to make clear that the desire is to possess. Literal repeats "covet".

decisions.choice: poner los ojos en
decisions.reason: Where the English Balanced says "set your heart on" for the second "covet", Spanish uses the idiom for fixing one's desire on something one means to have.

decisions.choice: jeter son dévolu sur
decisions.reason: Where the English Balanced says "set your heart on" for the second "covet", French uses the idiom for fixing one's desire on something one means to have.

decisions.choice: usimmezee mate
decisions.reason: Where the English Balanced says "set your heart on" for the second "covet", Swahili uses the idiom "kumezea mate" (to long for something one wants to have).

source.text: וְכָל־הָעָם֩ רֹאִ֨ים אֶת־הַקּוֹלֹ֜ת וְאֶת־הַלַּפִּידִ֗ם וְאֵת֙ ק֣וֹל הַשֹּׁפָ֔ר וְאֶת־הָהָ֖ר עָשֵׁ֑ן וַיַּ֤רְא הָעָם֙ וַיָּנֻ֔עוּ וַיַּֽעַמְד֖וּ מֵֽרָחֹֽק׃

records.literal_gloss: And all the people [were] seeing the thunders and the lightnings and [the] sound of the ram's horn and the mountain smoking; and saw the people, and they trembled and stood from a distance.

en.L: And all the people were seeing the thunderings and the lightnings and the sound of the ram's horn and the mountain smoking; and the people saw, and they trembled, and they stood far off.
en.B: All the people witnessed the thunder and the lightning, the blast of the ram's horn and the smoking mountain. When they saw it, they trembled and stood back at a distance.
en.R: All the people heard the thunder and the ram's horn, and they saw the lightning and the smoke on the mountain. When they saw it, they shook and stayed far back.

es.L: Y todo el pueblo estaba viendo los truenos y los relámpagos y el sonido del cuerno de carnero y el monte humeante; y el pueblo vio, y temblaron, y se quedaron de pie a lo lejos.
es.B: Todo el pueblo presenció los truenos y los relámpagos, el toque del cuerno de carnero y el monte envuelto en humo. Al verlo, temblaron y se mantuvieron a distancia.
es.R: Todo el pueblo oyó los truenos y el cuerno de carnero, y vio los relámpagos y el humo sobre el monte. Al ver todo eso, se pusieron a temblar y se quedaron bien lejos.

fr.L: Et tout le peuple voyait les tonnerres et les éclairs et le son de la corne de bélier et la montagne fumante ; et le peuple vit, et ils tremblèrent, et ils se tinrent au loin.
fr.B: Tout le peuple fut témoin du tonnerre et des éclairs, de la sonnerie de la corne de bélier et de la montagne qui fumait. À cette vue, ils tremblèrent et se tinrent à distance.
fr.R: Tout le peuple a entendu le tonnerre et la corne de bélier, et il a vu les éclairs et la fumée sur la montagne. En voyant cela, les gens ont tremblé et sont restés loin en arrière.

sw.L: Na watu wote walikuwa wakiona ngurumo na umeme na sauti ya pembe ya kondoo dume na mlima ukitoa moshi; na watu wakaona, wakatetemeka, wakasimama wakiwa mbali.
sw.B: Watu wote walishuhudia ngurumo na umeme, mlio wa pembe ya kondoo dume na mlima uliokuwa ukifuka moshi. Walipoona hayo, walitetemeka, wakajiweka mbali.
sw.R: Watu wote walisikia ngurumo na sauti ya pembe ya kondoo dume, wakaona umeme na moshi juu ya mlima. Walipoona hayo, walitetemeka, wakabaki mbali sana.

decisions.choice: seeing the thunders ... the sound: taking in all of it
decisions.reason: The people "see" sounds as well as sights. The verb here means to perceive with every sense: the thunder, the lightning, the horn and the smoke of 19:16-19.

decisions.choice: saw: some ancient witnesses read "were afraid"
decisions.reason: The Masoretic text reads "and the people saw". The two words differ in Hebrew only in their vowels, and the Samaritan Pentateuch and the Greek translation read "and the people were afraid". Either reading fits verse 20.

decisions.choice: trembled: shook, or drew back
decisions.reason: The verb means to shake or to move unsteadily. The people shook and kept their distance, as they had been warned (19:12, 21).

decisions.choice: heard ... saw
decisions.reason: Readable separates what was heard from what was seen. Literal and Balanced keep the single verb.

decisions.choice: pembe ya kondoo dume
decisions.reason: The shofar is a ram's horn, as the English says; "baragumu" and "tarumbeta" suggest a metal trumpet.

source.text: וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה דַּבֵּר־אַתָּ֥ה עִמָּ֖נוּ וְנִשְׁמָ֑עָה וְאַל־יְדַבֵּ֥ר עִמָּ֛נוּ אֱלֹהִ֖ים פֶּן־נָמֽוּת׃

records.literal_gloss: And they said to Moses, speak you with us and we will listen, and not let speak with us God, lest we die.

en.L: And they said to Moses, "You speak with us, and we will listen; but let not God speak with us, lest we die."
en.B: They said to Moses, "You speak to us, and we will listen. But God must not speak to us, or we will die."
en.R: They told Moses, "You talk to us, and we will listen. But do not let God talk to us. If {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does, we will die."

es.L: Y dijeron a Moisés: «Tú, habla con nosotros, y escucharemos; pero que Dios no hable con nosotros, no sea que muramos».
es.B: Le dijeron a Moisés: «Sé tú quien nos hable, y escucharemos. Pero Dios no debe hablarnos, o moriremos».
es.R: Le dijeron a Moisés: «Tú háblanos, y nosotros te haremos caso. Pero no dejes que Dios nos hable. Si {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} lo hace, nos moriremos».

fr.L: Et ils dirent à Moïse : « Toi, parle avec nous, et nous écouterons ; mais que Dieu ne parle pas avec nous, de crainte que nous ne mourions. »
fr.B: Ils dirent à Moïse : « C’est toi qui dois nous parler, et nous écouterons. Mais Dieu ne doit pas nous parler, sinon nous allons mourir. »
fr.R: Ils ont dit à Moïse : « Toi, parle-nous, et nous écouterons. Mais ne laisse pas Dieu nous parler. S’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} le fait, nous allons mourir. »

sw.L: Na wakamwambia Musa, "Wewe zungumza nasi, nasi tutasikiliza; lakini Mungu asizungumze nasi, ili tusife."
sw.B: Walimwambia Musa, "Wewe ndiye useme nasi, nasi tutakusikiliza. Lakini Mungu asiseme nasi, la sivyo tutakufa."
sw.R: Walimwambia Musa, "Wewe utuambie, nasi tutasikiliza. Lakini usimwache Mungu aongee nasi. Akiongea nasi, tutakufa."

decisions.choice: you speak with us: Moses is to stand between God and the people
decisions.reason: The word "you" is stressed. The people ask Moses to be their go-between, and God approves (Deuteronomy 5:23-28; 18:16-17).

decisions.choice: lest we die: the fear of meeting the holy God
decisions.reason: To hear God speak was thought to mean death (Deuteronomy 5:24-26; compare 33:20). The people had heard his voice and lived, yet they were afraid.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֣ה אֶל־הָעָם֮ אַל־תִּירָאוּ֒ כִּ֗י לְבַֽעֲבוּר֙ נַסּ֣וֹת אֶתְכֶ֔ם בָּ֖א הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וּבַעֲב֗וּר תִּהְיֶ֧ה יִרְאָת֛וֹ עַל־פְּנֵיכֶ֖ם לְבִלְתִּ֥י תֶחֱטָֽאוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Moses to the people, do not fear, for in order to test you has come God, and in order that may be his fear on your faces, so that not you will sin.

en.L: And Moses said to the people, "Do not fear; for in order to test you God has come, and in order that the fear of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} may be upon your faces, so that you will not sin."
en.B: Moses answered the people, "Do not be afraid. God has come to test you, and to put the fear of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} before your eyes, so that you will not sin."
en.R: Moses told the people, "Do not be afraid. God has come to test you. He wants you to fear and respect {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, so that you will not sin."

es.L: Y Moisés dijo al pueblo: «No {{plural_you:teman|temáis}}; pues es para {{plural_you:ponerlos|poneros}} a prueba que Dios ha venido, y para que el temor de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} esté sobre {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} rostros, a fin de que no {{plural_you:pequen|pequéis}}».
es.B: Moisés le respondió al pueblo: «No {{plural_you:se asusten|os asustéis}}. Dios ha venido para {{plural_you:probarlos|probaros}} y para que {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} temor esté siempre ante {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} ojos, de modo que no {{plural_you:pequen|pequéis}}».
es.R: Moisés le dijo al pueblo: «No {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo. Dios ha venido a {{plural_you:probarlos|probaros}}. Quiere que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} {{plural_you:teman|temáis}} y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} {{plural_you:respeten|respetéis}}, para que no {{plural_you:pequen|pequéis}}».

fr.L: Et Moïse dit au peuple : « Ne craignez pas ; car c’est afin de vous éprouver que Dieu est venu, et afin que la crainte de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} soit sur vos faces, pour que vous ne péchiez pas. »
fr.B: Moïse répondit au peuple : « N’ayez pas peur. Dieu est venu pour vous éprouver, et pour que la crainte de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} reste devant vos yeux, afin que vous ne péchiez pas. »
fr.R: Moïse a dit au peuple : « N’ayez pas peur. Dieu est venu pour vous mettre à l’épreuve. Il veut que vous {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} craigniez et que vous {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} respectiez ; ainsi vous ne pécherez pas. »

sw.L: Na Musa akawaambia watu, "Msiogope; kwa maana ili kuwajaribu Mungu amekuja, na ili hofu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} iwe juu ya nyuso zenu, ili msitende dhambi."
sw.B: Musa aliwajibu watu, "Msiogope. Mungu amekuja kuwapima, na kuweka kicho {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}} mbele ya macho yenu, ili msitende dhambi."
sw.R: Musa aliwaambia watu, "Msiogope. Mungu amekuja kuwajaribu. Anataka mumche na kumheshimu, ili msitende dhambi."

decisions.choice: test: prove, to show and to train loyalty
decisions.reason: God tests his people to show what is in their hearts and to teach them to trust and obey (15:25; 16:4; Deuteronomy 8:2).

decisions.choice: do not fear ... the fear of him: terror set against reverence
decisions.reason: The same root is used twice. The people need not be terrified that God will kill them; but they are to keep the fear of God, the awe and reverence that keep a person from sin (Proverbs 16:6).

decisions.choice: on your faces: always before you
decisions.reason: The fear of God is to be before their eyes, present and remembered.

decisions.choice: fear and respect him
decisions.reason: Readable says "fear and respect" to show that this fear is reverence, not terror.

decisions.choice: kicho (B); kumcha (R)
decisions.reason: Verse 20 sets terror against reverence (m2). Literal keeps "hofu" for both, as the Hebrew uses one root; Balanced and Readable use "kicho" and "kumcha", the words for the reverent fear of God, so that the second fear is not read as terror.

source.text: וַיַּעֲמֹ֥ד הָעָ֖ם מֵרָחֹ֑ק וּמֹשֶׁה֙ נִגַּ֣שׁ אֶל־הָֽעֲרָפֶ֔ל אֲשֶׁר־שָׁ֖ם הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And stood the people from a distance, and Moses drew near to the thick darkness where there [was] God.

en.L: And the people stood far off, and Moses drew near to the thick darkness where God [was].
en.B: So the people kept their distance, and Moses went up close to the thick darkness where God was.
en.R: The people stayed far away. But Moses went near the dark cloud where God was.

es.L: Y el pueblo se quedó a lo lejos, y Moisés se acercó a la densa oscuridad donde [estaba] Dios.
es.B: Así que el pueblo se mantuvo a distancia, y Moisés se acercó a la espesa oscuridad en la que estaba Dios.
es.R: El pueblo se quedó lejos. Pero Moisés se acercó a la nube oscura donde estaba Dios.

fr.L: Et le peuple se tint au loin, et Moïse s’approcha de l’obscurité épaisse où [était] Dieu.
fr.B: Le peuple resta donc à distance, tandis que Moïse s’avança tout près de l’épaisse obscurité où se trouvait Dieu.
fr.R: Les gens sont restés loin. Mais Moïse s’est approché du nuage sombre où Dieu était.

sw.L: Na watu wakasimama kwa mbali, naye Musa akasogea karibu na giza nene ambamo Mungu [alikuwa].
sw.B: Basi watu walibaki mbali, na Musa akasogea karibu kabisa na giza zito alimokuwa Mungu.
sw.R: Watu walikaa mbali. Lakini Musa akaenda karibu na wingu jeusi ambamo Mungu alikuwa.

decisions.choice: thick darkness: the dark cloud that hid God
decisions.reason: The word names deep darkness, a dense cloud (19:9, 16). God is present in it and hidden by it (Deuteronomy 4:11; 5:22; 1 Kings 8:12).

decisions.choice: Moses drew near: the one who stands between
decisions.reason: Moses goes where the people may not, as they had asked (verse 19; 24:2, 18).

decisions.choice: the dark cloud
decisions.reason: Readable explains the thick darkness as a cloud, as 19:9 and 19:16 describe it.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה כֹּ֥ה תֹאמַ֖ר אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אַתֶּ֣ם רְאִיתֶ֔ם כִּ֚י מִן־הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם דִּבַּ֖רְתִּי עִמָּכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, thus you shall say to [the] sons of Israel, you have seen that from the heavens I have spoken with you.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Thus you shall say to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel: 'You yourselves have seen that from the heavens I have spoken with you.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Say this to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}: 'You saw with your own eyes that I spoke with you from heaven.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Give the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} this message: 'You saw how I spoke to you from heaven.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo a Moisés: «Esto dirás a los hijos de Israel: “{{plural_you:Ustedes mismos han visto|Vosotros mismos habéis visto}} que desde los cielos he hablado con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo a Moisés: «Di esto a los israelitas: “{{plural_you:Ustedes vieron|Vosotros visteis}} con {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} propios ojos que {{plural_you:les|os}} hablé desde el cielo.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo a Moisés: «Dales este mensaje a los israelitas: “{{plural_you:Ustedes vieron|Vosotros visteis}} cómo {{plural_you:les|os}} hablé desde el cielo.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à Moïse : « Ainsi tu diras aux {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël : “Vous-mêmes, vous avez vu que des cieux j’ai parlé avec vous.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à Moïse : « Dis ceci aux {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} : “Vous l’avez vu de vos yeux : c’est du ciel que je vous ai parlé.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit à Moïse : « Transmets ce message aux {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} : “Vous avez vu comment je vous ai parlé du ciel.

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Musa, "Hivi ndivyo utakavyowaambia wana wa Israeli, 'Ninyi mmejionea wenyewe ya kuwa kutoka mbinguni nimesema nanyi.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimwambia Musa, "Waambie Waisraeli hivi: 'Mliona kwa macho yenu wenyewe kwamba nilisema nanyi kutoka mbinguni.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimwambia Musa, "Wapelekee Waisraeli ujumbe huu: 'Mliona jinsi nilivyosema nanyi kutoka mbinguni.

decisions.choice: you have seen that I have spoken from heaven: the people are witnesses
decisions.reason: The people heard God's voice themselves (Deuteronomy 4:36; 5:4). That is the ground for the laws that follow.

decisions.choice: a long speech begins here
decisions.reason: God's words from here to 23:33 form one speech, probably the "book of the covenant" read to the people in 24:7. It opens with laws on worship and the altar (verses 23-26).

source.text: לֹ֥א תַעֲשׂ֖וּן אִתִּ֑י אֱלֹ֤הֵי כֶ֨סֶף֙ וֵאלֹהֵ֣י זָהָ֔ב לֹ֥א תַעֲשׂ֖וּ לָכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Not you shall make with me gods of silver and gods of gold; not you shall make for yourselves.

en.L: You shall not make with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} gods of silver and gods of gold; you shall not make [them] for yourselves.
en.B: You shall not make gods to share {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} place; you shall not make yourselves gods of silver or gold.
en.R: Do not make any gods to stand next to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Do not make idols of silver or gold for yourselves.

es.L: No {{plural_you:harán|haréis}} conmigo dioses de plata y dioses de oro; no [los] {{plural_you:harán|haréis}} para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: No {{plural_you:se harán|os haréis}} dioses que compartan {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} lugar; no {{plural_you:se fabricarán|os fabricaréis}} dioses de plata ni de oro.
es.R: No {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}} dioses para ponerlos junto a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. No {{plural_you:se fabriquen|os fabriquéis}} ídolos de plata o de oro.

fr.L: Vous ne ferez pas avec {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} des dieux d’argent et des dieux d’or ; vous ne [les] ferez pas pour vous.
fr.B: Vous ne ferez pas de dieux pour partager {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} place ; vous ne vous fabriquerez pas de dieux d’argent ni d’or.
fr.R: Ne faites pas de dieux à placer à côté de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. Ne vous fabriquez pas d’idoles en argent ou en or.

sw.L: Hamtafanya pamoja {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} miungu ya fedha na miungu ya dhahabu; hamtajifanyia [miungu hiyo].
sw.B: Msifanye miungu ya kushiriki nafasi {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}; msijitengenezee miungu ya fedha wala ya dhahabu.
sw.R: Msitengeneze miungu yoyote ya kusimama kando {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. Msijitengenezee sanamu za fedha au za dhahabu.

decisions.choice: with me ... gods of silver: where the sentence divides
alternatives: You shall not make gods of silver alongside me, nor gods of gold for yourselves
decisions.reason: The Hebrew accents divide the verse after "with me": "You shall not make [anything] with me; gods of silver and gods of gold you shall not make for yourselves." The words can also be read "You shall not make gods of silver to be with me". Either way no image may stand beside God.

decisions.choice: gods of gold: the sin of the golden calf
decisions.reason: The same words return when Israel makes the golden calf (32:4, 31).

decisions.choice: plural "ustedes" forms in verses 20 and 22-23, singular "tú" elsewhere
decisions.reason: The ten words speak to Israel as one person ("tú"), as the Hebrew does. Moses in verse 20 and God in verses 22-23 address the people in the plural, so Spanish switches to "ustedes" there, with the plural_you setting; verses 24-26 return to the singular. "Conmigo" takes no deity pronoun span, as "conmigo" and "contigo" take none elsewhere in the Spanish.

decisions.choice: "vous" in verses 20 and 22-23, "tu" elsewhere
decisions.reason: The ten words speak to Israel as one person ("tu"), as the Hebrew does. Moses in verse 20 and God in verses 22-23 address the people in the plural, so French says "vous" there; verses 24-26 return to the singular.

decisions.choice: plural ("msifanye", "ninyi") in verses 20 and 22-23, singular elsewhere
decisions.reason: The ten words speak to Israel as one person ("usiue"), as the Hebrew does. Moses in verse 20 and God in verses 22-23 address the people in the plural, so Swahili uses the plural there; verses 24-26 return to the singular.

source.text: מִזְבַּ֣ח אֲדָמָה֮ תַּעֲשֶׂה־לִּי֒ וְזָבַחְתָּ֣ עָלָ֗יו אֶת־עֹלֹתֶ֨יךָ֙ וְאֶת־שְׁלָמֶ֔יךָ אֶת־צֹֽאנְךָ֖ וְאֶת־בְּקָרֶ֑ךָ בְּכָל־הַמָּקוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַזְכִּ֣יר אֶת־שְׁמִ֔י אָב֥וֹא אֵלֶ֖יךָ וּבֵרַכְתִּֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: An altar of earth you shall make for me, and you shall sacrifice on it your burnt offerings and your peace offerings, your flock and your herd; in every place where I cause to be remembered my name I will come to you and I will bless you.

en.L: An altar of earth you shall make for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and you shall sacrifice on it your burnt offerings and your peace offerings, your flock and your herd; in every place where I cause {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name to be remembered, I will come to you and I will bless you.
en.B: You are to make an altar of earth for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and on it sacrifice your burnt offerings and your fellowship offerings, from your flocks and your herds. Wherever I cause {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name to be remembered, I will come to you and bless you.
en.R: Build {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} an altar of earth. Offer on it your burnt offerings and fellowship offerings, animals from your flocks and herds. Wherever I choose to have people remember {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, I will come to you and bless you.

es.L: Un altar de tierra {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} harás, y sacrificarás sobre él tus holocaustos y tus sacrificios de paz, tu ganado menor y tu ganado mayor; en todo lugar donde yo haga que se recuerde {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre, vendré hacia ti y te bendeciré.
es.B: Harás para {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} un altar de tierra, y en él ofrecerás tus holocaustos y tus sacrificios de paz, de tus rebaños de ovejas y cabras y de tus manadas de vacas. Dondequiera que yo haga recordar {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre, iré a tu encuentro y te bendeciré.
es.R: Construye un altar de tierra para {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Ofrece sobre él tus holocaustos y tus sacrificios de paz, animales de tus rebaños y de tus manadas. Dondequiera que yo elija que la gente recuerde {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre, vendré a ti y te bendeciré.

fr.L: Un autel de terre, tu {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} [le] feras, et tu sacrifieras sur lui tes holocaustes et tes sacrifices de communion, ton petit bétail et ton gros bétail ; en tout lieu où je ferai rappeler {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom, je viendrai vers toi et te bénirai.
fr.B: Tu {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} feras un autel de terre, et tu y offriras en sacrifice tes holocaustes et tes sacrifices de communion, pris de ton petit et de ton gros bétail. Partout où je ferai rappeler {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom, je viendrai vers toi et je te bénirai.
fr.R: Construis-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} un autel de terre. Offre dessus tes holocaustes et tes sacrifices de communion, des animaux de tes troupeaux de moutons, de chèvres et de bœufs. Partout où je déciderai que l’on se souvienne de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom, je viendrai vers toi et je te bénirai.

sw.L: Madhabahu ya udongo utanifanyia, na utatoa dhabihu juu yake sadaka zako za kuteketezwa na sadaka zako za amani, kondoo wako na ng'ombe wako; katika kila mahali nitakapolifanya jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} likumbukwe, nitakuja kwako na kukubariki.
sw.B: Utanijengea madhabahu ya udongo, na juu yake utoe sadaka zako za kuteketezwa na sadaka zako za amani, kutoka katika makundi yako ya kondoo na mbuzi na ya ng'ombe. Mahali popote nitakapolifanya jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} likumbukwe, nitakujia na kukubariki.
sw.R: Nijengee madhabahu ya udongo. Toa juu yake sadaka zako za kuteketezwa na sadaka za amani, wanyama kutoka katika makundi yako ya kondoo, mbuzi na ng'ombe. Popote nitakapochagua watu walikumbuke jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, nitakuja kwako na kukubariki.

decisions.choice: an altar of earth: a plain, unworked altar
decisions.reason: The altar was to be heaped up from soil or, as the next verse allows, from uncut stones: simple, made by the worshipers, with no carving or art.

decisions.choice: where I cause my name to be remembered: God chooses where he is worshiped
decisions.reason: God himself decides where he will be called on, and there he comes and blesses. The ancestors built altars where God had appeared to them (Genesis 12:7-8; 28:18-22), and later God chose one place for his name (Deuteronomy 12:5, 11).

decisions.choice: in every place where I cause: the Samaritan Pentateuch reads "in the place where I have caused"
alternatives: in the place where I have caused my name to be remembered
decisions.reason: The Samaritan Pentateuch has "in the place" and a past-tense verb, pointing to one chosen site. The Masoretic text, followed here, says "every place".

decisions.choice: fellowship offerings ... flocks and herds
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "fellowship offerings", Literal "peace offerings", as in chapters 25-31. The flock is sheep and goats, the herd cattle.

decisions.choice: ton petit bétail et ton gros bétail
decisions.reason: The flock (sheep and goats) and the herd (cattle) are the two kinds of livestock; French "petit bétail" and "gros bétail" name both groups. Readable lists the animals.

source.text: וְאִם־מִזְבַּ֤ח אֲבָנִים֙ תַּֽעֲשֶׂה־לִּ֔י לֹֽא־תִבְנֶ֥ה אֶתְהֶ֖ן גָּזִ֑ית כִּ֧י חַרְבְּךָ֛ הֵנַ֥פְתָּ עָלֶ֖יהָ וַתְּחַֽלְלֶֽהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And if an altar of stones you make for me, not you shall build them hewn; for your tool you have wielded on it and you have profaned it.

en.L: And if an altar of stones you make for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, you shall not build them [as] hewn [stone]; for [if] you have wielded your tool upon it, you have profaned it.
en.B: If you make {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} an altar of stones, do not build it from cut stones. Once you swing your tool over it, you rob it of its holiness.
en.R: If you build an altar of stones for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, do not cut or shape the stones. If you use a tool on them, the altar will no longer be holy.

es.L: Y si un altar de piedras {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} haces, no las edificarás [como piedra] labrada; porque [si] has blandido tu herramienta sobre él, lo has profanado.
es.B: Si {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} haces un altar de piedras, no lo construyas con piedras labradas. En cuanto blandas tu herramienta sobre él, le habrás quitado su santidad.
es.R: Si construyes un altar de piedras para {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, no cortes ni des forma a las piedras. Si usas una herramienta en ellas, el altar ya no será santo.

fr.L: Et si tu {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} fais un autel de pierres, tu ne les bâtiras pas [en pierre] taillée ; car [si] tu as brandi ton outil sur lui, tu l’as profané.
fr.B: Si tu {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} fais un autel de pierres, ne le construis pas en pierres taillées. Dès que tu lèves ton outil sur elles, tu le prives de sa sainteté.
fr.R: Si tu construis pour {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} un autel de pierres, ne taille pas les pierres et ne leur donne pas de forme. Si tu utilises un outil sur elles, l’autel ne sera plus saint.

sw.L: Na kama madhabahu ya mawe utanifanyia, hutaijenga [kwa] mawe yaliyokatwa; kwa kuwa [ikiwa] umepitisha kifaa chako juu yake, umeinajisi.
sw.B: Kama utanijengea madhabahu ya mawe, isijengwe kwa mawe yaliyochongwa. Mara unapopitisha kifaa chako juu yake, unaiondolea utakatifu wake.
sw.R: Ukinijengea madhabahu ya mawe, usiyakate wala usiyachonge mawe hayo. Ukitumia kifaa juu yake, madhabahu hiyo haitakuwa takatifu tena.

decisions.choice: tool: a blade, an iron tool for shaping stone
decisions.reason: The word usually means a sword. Here it is any iron blade or chisel used to dress stone (Deuteronomy 27:5-6; Joshua 8:31).

decisions.choice: profaned: made common, no longer fit for God
decisions.reason: To profane is to take away what is holy and make it ordinary. Human shaping of the stones would spoil an altar meant to be as God made it.

source.text: וְלֹֽא־תַעֲלֶ֥ה בְמַעֲלֹ֖ת עַֽל־מִזְבְּחִ֑י אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹֽא־תִגָּלֶ֥ה עֶרְוָתְךָ֖ עָלָֽיו׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And not you shall go up by steps to my altar, that not will be uncovered your nakedness on it.

en.L: And you shall not go up by steps to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} altar, that your nakedness may not be uncovered on it.
en.B: Do not climb to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} altar by steps, so that your nakedness is not exposed there.
en.R: Do not use steps to go up to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} altar. Then no one will see your body uncovered there.

es.L: Y no subirás por escalones a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} altar, para que no quede al descubierto tu desnudez sobre él.
es.B: Para subir a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} altar no pongas escalones, no sea que tu desnudez quede expuesta allí.
es.R: No uses escalones para subir a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} altar. Así nadie verá allí tu cuerpo descubierto.

fr.L: Et tu ne monteras pas par des marches à {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} autel, afin que ta nudité ne soit pas dévoilée sur lui.
fr.B: Ne gravis pas de marches pour accéder à {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} autel, de peur que ta nudité n’y soit exposée.
fr.R: N’utilise pas de marches pour monter à {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} autel. Ainsi, personne ne verra ton corps découvert à cet endroit.

sw.L: Na hutapanda kwa ngazi kwenye madhabahu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, ili uchi wako usije ukafunuka juu yake.
sw.B: Usipande madhabahu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} kwa kutumia ngazi, ili uchi wako usionekane hapo.
sw.R: Usitumie ngazi kupanda kwenye madhabahu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. Hivyo hakuna mtu atakayeuona mwili wako ukiwa wazi hapo.

decisions.choice: steps to my altar: a raised altar reached by a stair
decisions.reason: A worshiper in a short robe or kilt climbing high steps could expose himself to those below. Later the priests wore linen undergarments for the same reason (28:42-43).

decisions.choice: nakedness uncovered: the body exposed, a shame before God
decisions.reason: Worship at God's altar must not expose the worshiper's body (Leviticus 18:6-7 uses the same word).
